m-cocoa|2026-06-23|b5b69e7f|5279ab16d4ea.title: 5 “Significant redevelopment opportunities exist at several sites in the Village, including Bank of America, the former City Hall and Sun Trust Bank sites.” Redevelopment of the subject property will transform a severely underutilized block and create new housing options for residents. At build-out, approximately 350-400 residents are expected. New proposed retail uses will revitalize the Village and increase pedestrian activity along Brevard Avenue. Within the enclosed parking area, twenty-five (25) public parking spaces will be provided and available to all visitors. CM Carlucci expressed appreciation for the work DIA does. 
CM Salem asked about the CRA funds. Guy Parola, DIA, said the Northbank CRA fund has roughly $18 million and the Southbank CRA has around $7.5 million. 
CM Salem talked about the elimination of future completion grants.

Colin Tarbert, DIA, gave a presentation about projects downtown. Mr. Tarbert offered an update on various projects in progress, including Gateway N7 (with the Publix), Riverfront restaurant with Atlas, Hotel Merrydelle, and Snyder Memorial.

Mr. Tarbert mentioned the Culinary Institute of America and the potential opening of a campus in Jacksonville, that was before the CIA Board in recent weeks. He said that there has not been a formal announcement on the new campus location yet. 

CM Carlucci asked about Gateway N7 (with the Publix) and the incentives involved. Mr. Tarbert explained the mixed use project, that overall is roughly $140 million and includes REV and retail enhancement funding and a completion grant around $28 million. Mr. Tarbert talked about the timeline for that project. CM Carlucci asked about the impact from reduced City revenue if the referendum to reduce property taxes is approved by voters in November. Mr. Tarbert highlighted the importance of momentum as related to downtown projects. 

Mr. Tarbert talked about an affordable housing project on the Southbank, Artea on Broadcast Place. He described the proposed up-front REV grant funding ($6.3 million) and the contributions from the Southbank CRA and from the General Fund. MEASUREMENT FOCUS, BASIS OF ACCOUNTING, AND FINANCIAL STATEMENT PRESENTATION Basis of accounting refers to when revenues, expenditures or expenses are recognized in the accounts and reported in the financial statements. It relates to the timing of the measurements made, regardless of the measurement focus applied. The government-wide financial statements are report ed using the economic resources measurement focus and the accrual basis of accounting. Revenues are recorded when earned and expenses are recorded when a liability is incurred, regardless of the timing of related cash flows. Governmental fund financial statements are reported using the current financial resources measurement focus and the modified accrual basis of accounting. Revenues are recognized as soon as they are both measurable and available. Revenues are considered to be available when they are collectible within the current period or soon enough thereafter to pay liabilities of the current period. For this purpose, the government considers revenues to be available if they are collected within 60 days of the end of the current fiscal period.
